questions.prompt: Is a need identical to a proposed solution?
questions.answer: No; several options may meet the same need.

questions.prompt: Does emotional intensity create an obligation?
questions.answer: No; obligations depend on agreements, authority and actual duties.
It respects autonomy and communicates legitimate requirements transparently.
When coercion, threats or power imbalance creates risk.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Separates needs from preferred solutions and coercive demands, respects duties and identifies feasible alternatives.
scoring.transfer: Build a fictional need-options table with three possible solutions, a consent check and a fallback. Rewrite a controlling demand into a respectful request or a self-directed decision. Explain when formal or specialist support is preferable to direct communication.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
